cuts.raw_narration: A boy with glasses in a school uniform, Shinichi, stands in his family's dining room the morning after something happened to him. He clenches and spreads the fingers of his right hand, examining it with a puzzled look, and tells his mother his hand feels kind of numb. She brushes it off, saying he probably fell asleep with his headphone cord wrapped around it.

That night, back in his bedroom, Shinichi is jolted awake by his own right hand talking to him. He sits up dazed at his desk as the hand calmly announces it has been studying, and in disbelief he asks what it is — is it an alien, is that wormy thing from last night what it really looks like?

To show him what it can do, the creature — Migi — reshapes his right hand in front of his face: it stretches into a fleshy stalk, splits open to reveal needle-like teeth and a tiny screaming human head, then settles with an eyeball on a stem and a human mouth. Shinichi recoils, sweating, and asks why on earth this is happening to him.

Shaken, Shinichi says he really should go to a hospital and have it cut off. Migi warns that removing it would kill them both — it survives on the nutrients in his bloodstream, and Shinichi would lose his right hand in the process.

The next morning at the breakfast counter, the news behind him plays footage of a string of gruesome killings — a mother and daughter mutilated overnight, someone else decapitated, another hacked up and left hanging. Shinichi sits frozen, the pieces of what Migi really is lining up in his head.

Later, walking through a residential neighborhood, Migi suddenly goes rigid on Shinichi's arm and its stalk-eye extends: it senses one of its own species nearby, about two hundred meters away. Shinichi stops in the street, stunned that there's more of them out there.

Migi steers him down a shadowed alley. Around the corner Shinichi finds the source: a small dog in a green coat, hunched over another dead animal in a spreading pool of blood. It lifts its head, addresses Migi like a fellow parasite, and says its own host is not optimal. Migi orders Shinichi to run — and the dog transforms mid-lunge into a winged, monstrous shape.

Shinichi stumbles backwards over a guardrail in panic while Migi warps his right hand into a bladed, single-eyed weapon. Migi tells him there's no choice — if the creature kills Shinichi, Migi dies too — and meets the beast head-on.

In the aftermath, the winged parasite lies dead on the pavement beside them. Migi, calm as ever, coolly explains that research is the reason it won. Shinichi looks down at his own right hand and mutters that he's talking to an insect — one that doesn't have a shred of sympathy. Over a final image, a voice returns to where the story began: not long ago, someone on earth had a passing thought — all life is sacred, and must therefore be protected.
